symbols.name: RECORD_EMBED_CHARS
doc: The most characters of one announcement that go into its own vector; I use the circulars' whole-document rule.

symbols.name: recordEmbeddingText
symbols.sig: export function recordEmbeddingText(title: string, contentText: string | null | undefined, pdfText?: string | null): string
doc: The text an announcement's own vector is made from: its title, its body text, and the start of the text of its PDF. I include the PDF so that an announcement that is only a title and a PDF is found by what the PDF says, not by its title alone. Plain text, never HTML. Empty when there is nothing at all.

symbols.name: embedAnnouncement
symbols.sig: export async function embedAnnouncement( announcementId: number, title: string, contentText: string | null | undefined, pdfText?: string | null,): Promise<boolean>
doc: I compute and store the semantic embedding for a single announcement here.

It embeds `title + contentText + the start of its PDF's text` (plain text, never HTML), matching the circular pipeline's 768-dim Gemini path. I write the normalized vector into announcement.embedding as a pgvector literal.
`pdfText` left out = read from the PDF index if there is one (an edit of the title or body must not forget what the PDF says).
Non-throwing: a Gemini failure logs and returns false so the caller (create / edit) can still succeed. The announcement is simply not yet searchable and will be indexed on its next save.

symbols.name: embedAnnouncementById
symbols.sig: export async function embedAnnouncementById(announcementId: number): Promise<boolean>
doc: The same, for an announcement known only by its id (I read its title and body from the database).
